review_scope: Round 2 checks versioned arXiv sources and selected upstream source declarations. New families have per-family repository pins. Source-reported results are not independently verified proofs, and this is not an exhaustive literature or in-flight formalization audit. Unannotated legacy dossiers remain not rechecked. Proposed subproblems remain proposals.

families.title: What completes the Thue-Morse reduced abelian recurrence?
families.question: With R(2n+1) = R(n+1) proved, can the even-index values be described by an explicit recurrence, and is the resulting reduced abelian complexity sequence non-k-automatic for every integer k >= 2?
families.foothold: The proved all-start odd recurrence and the bridge from literal run compression to Parikh classes fix the exact object whose even values remain to be studied.
families.gap: The odd recurrence supplies no rule for R(4n). Section 3 separately asks for equation (11), the sign of its nonzero difference, and non-k-automaticity. None follows just by iterating the odd theorem.
families.next_step: Work with the same all-start class definitions and derive a candidate relation for the even-length run codes.
families.success: An all-index even recurrence, a proof or counterexample for equation (11), or a theorem deciding the stated automaticity question. Finite samples are evidence only.

source.title: Reduced complexities for sequences over finite alphabets
source.locator: Section 3: equation (11), the even-index recursion and non-k-automaticity
source.note: The odd recurrence is already proved in our result. These are the distinct remaining questions in the cited version, not an assertion that all later literature and ongoing work have been exhaustively checked.

targets.title: An exact even-length class relation
targets.question: Can the difference R(4n+2)-R(4n) be characterized for every n >= 1, including its sign when nonzero?
targets.gap: Equation (11) predicts only the absolute difference from Thue-Morse symbols. It does not determine its sign or R(4n).
targets.next_step: Translate even factors to run codes, separating the two starting parities, and test which class endpoints survive the reflection used in the odd proof.
targets.success: A proved relation for all natural starts and all n >= 1, with equation (11) and any stronger sign claim stated separately.

targets.title: Does the complexity sequence escape every finite-output automaton?
targets.question: Can one prove that R(n), for n >= 1, is not k-automatic for any k >= 2?
targets.gap: The constant subsequence R(2^j+1)=3 does not imply boundedness or automaticity of the whole sequence.
targets.next_step: Search for and then prove an unbounded subsequence, or identify another obstruction to a finite k-kernel.
targets.success: An unboundedness theorem or another rigorous obstruction covering each k >= 2; a finite graph or sampled values alone do not suffice.

families.title: What survives of the Pochhammer interval conjecture in higher degree?
families.question: After the degree-two counterexample to c_(2k)(a) < 2a, is M_(2k)(a) still a single symmetric interval for all k >= 2 and a > 0, and what can be proved about the sequence of its left endpoint radii?
families.foothold: The actual Pochhammer operator, all-complex-root interval condition and exact quadratic classification are already formalized. The failure of the strict bound leaves the interval shape and degree comparisons as separate questions.
families.gap: The original conjunction is false. Its interval and monotonicity clauses must be tested independently, without importing the disproved bound or assuming that a > 1/24 repairs every degree.
families.next_step: Start with degree four, derive the transformed coefficients exactly, and isolate parameter ranges with certified real-root counts.
families.success: An exact degree-four classification or a checked counterexample to interval connectedness or monotonicity; any general statement must retain its parameter conditions.

source.title: Polynomially Deformed Normalized Pochhammer Sequences Having Generating Functions With Only Real Non-positive Zeros
source.locator: Example 6.4 and Conjecture 6.5: interval, monotonicity and limiting-value clauses
source.note: Our quadratic result refutes the original strict upper bound. This family asks about the remaining clauses separately. Degree-two root-radius progress in upstream QuadraticRadii addresses other questions and is not an all-even-degree result.

targets.title: A certified degree-four admissible interval
targets.question: For each positive a, is the set of t for which every root of L_a((X+t)^4) lies in [-1,0] a single interval?
targets.gap: The quadratic discriminant argument does not classify all four complex roots of the quartic.
targets.next_step: Construct L_a((X+t)^4) from the same basis action and use exact root isolation or a Sturm certificate, including repeated roots and endpoints.
targets.success: A proved parameter classification or an exact disconnected-set counterexample, with every complex root accounted for.

targets.title: Compare the degree-two and degree-four radii
targets.question: With c_(2k)(a) defined independently from the admissible set, does c2(a) <= c4(a) hold for every a > 0?
targets.gap: Monotonicity was bundled with a false strict bound in the source conjecture. Its validity has to be established separately.
targets.next_step: Use the proved c2 closed form as a baseline for the exact quartic endpoint, preserving infimum existence and boundedness obligations.
targets.success: A universal comparison or a certified parameter counterexample. Later degree comparisons and the limiting value remain separate targets.

families.title: Does the greedy formula hold for the separate g+1 seed family?
families.question: For every g >= 2, does the literal greedy three-sumfree sequence starting 1,g,g+1 have the membership formula in published Conjecture 16, with modulus 10g+3 and its two residue intervals?
families.foothold: Conjecture 17 establishes a proof route from explicit accepted blocks through forbidden sums to the literal least-next-entry process.
families.gap: Putting d=1 into Conjecture 17 violates its hypothesis d>=2. The g+1 family has different exceptional values, modulus and two residue intervals; its universal claim needs a new proof.
families.next_step: Encode the published Conjecture 16 candidate and prove its accepted and forbidden block statements uniformly in g.
families.success: The exact membership equivalence for every natural g>=2 and every positive candidate value, linked to the literal greedy sequence, or an exact counterexample.

source.title: Using Walnut to solve problems from the OEIS
source.locator: The g+1 third-seed conjecture; numbered Conjecture 16 in JIS 28 (2025), Article 25.3.8
source.note: The source gives fixed-parameter checks, distinct from the universal conjecture. Published Conjecture 16 and our solved Conjecture 17 are separate families. Numbering differs in the early arXiv version.

targets.title: Accepted blocks and forbidden sums for g+1
targets.question: Can the candidate set with exceptions 1,2g+1,6g+1 and residue intervals [g,2g] and [6g+2,7g+1] modulo 10g+3 be characterized by restricted triple sums?
targets.gap: The single-interval periodic decomposition from Conjecture 17 cannot be reused without handling both new intervals and all cross-sums.
targets.next_step: Prove three-sumfreeness and explicit representations of every excluded later value, separating the initial segment from periodic translates.
targets.success: A uniform accepted/forbidden partition for every g>=2 that preserves the requirement of three distinct earlier summands.

targets.title: Connect the candidate to the least-next-entry sequence
targets.question: Does the new candidate describe every term selected by the literal greedy process from 1,g,g+1?
targets.gap: A sumfree candidate by itself does not prove that the greedy algorithm generates it.
targets.next_step: Adapt the prefix invariant and uniqueness argument to the new accepted/forbidden partition, including the seed boundary.
targets.success: An all-parameter membership theorem matching Conjecture 16. Verified samples remain examples, not the universal result.

families.title: Is the 22-state base-4 golden-ratio DFAO minimal?
families.question: Must every leading-zero-invariant DFAO that produces the correct golden-ratio digit on all Zeckendorf encodings of 4^i have at least 22 states?
families.foothold: Canonical digits, exact ordering and the Beatty bridge supply arithmetic inputs without floating-point phi.
families.gap: Minimizing the full valid-input machine does not establish minimality on the sparse powers-of-four language.
families.next_step: Verify the published transition table and exact input/output conventions before searching for a smaller machine.
families.success: An all-powers correctness proof for a machine with at most 21 states, or a sound lower-bound certificate excluding every such machine.

targets.title: A sparse-language distinguishability certificate
targets.question: Can 22 prefixes be found such that every pair has a common suffix making both completed words legal power inputs with different required outputs?
targets.gap: Each separation witness must constrain both words inside the sparse domain. Full-language Myhill-Nerode witnesses may be irrelevant here.
targets.next_step: Build exact labelled prefix trees; search for a 22-clique of pairwise incompatible prefixes and retain both completed power inputs for every edge.
targets.success: A checked finite incompatibility certificate plus a proof that it forces 22 distinct states. Failure to find a clique leaves other lower-bound methods open.

targets.title: A finite, replayable 21-state UNSAT obstruction
targets.question: Can a finite set of exact power-input digit constraints already exclude all DFAOs with at most 21 states under the chosen conventions?
targets.gap: A solver verdict needs a proof-checking and encoding-soundness bridge. A SAT candidate still requires all-powers verification.
targets.next_step: Encode a bounded labelled sample, export an independently checkable UNSAT certificate, and account for state renaming and leading-zero invariance.
targets.success: Every globally correct DFAO must satisfy the sample; a sound finite UNSAT certificate therefore proves the lower bound. Finite sample completeness is unnecessary for this direction.

families.title: Can four mutually unbiased bases exist in dimension six?
families.question: Does a family of four orthonormal bases of complex dimension six exist with every cross-basis squared inner product equal to 1/6?
families.foothold: Rank-one contexts, overlaps and complementary-context identities express nearby exact geometry.
families.gap: Conditional tomography identities assume the family. A complete seven-basis design identity does not automatically constrain a four-basis family.
families.next_step: Establish the exact basis/context correspondence, then express all cross-basis compatibility equations in one coordinate system.
families.success: An exact four-basis construction or a nonexistence proof covering the whole feasible set, with no unverified classification assumed.

targets.title: An exact basis-to-projector bridge
targets.question: Can orthonormal bases modulo individual phases be represented faithfully as labelled complete rank-one projector contexts, preserving the MUB overlap condition?
targets.gap: Rank-one, completeness, orthogonality, labelling and phase equivalence all need explicit hypotheses.
targets.next_step: Formalize both directions and prove trace(P_i Q_j) = |inner(v_i,w_j)|^2, using the repository context definitions.
targets.success: A proved correspondence at dimension six that translates the four-basis feasible set without adding a two-design assumption.

targets.title: A certificate for joint Hadamard compatibility
targets.question: Can an independently verified order-six Hadamard parameterization support a complete exact exclusion or construction for three Hadamards relative to the identity basis?
targets.gap: A classification claim alone leaves pairwise and joint compatibility to prove. Numerical near-solutions do not satisfy exact equations.
targets.next_step: First check parameterization coverage and exceptional branches, then express every required cross-Gram modulus equation and seek exact certificates.
targets.success: An exact solution or branch-covering exclusion with proved coverage. Treat the dossier-mentioned classification preprint as unverified input until checked.

targets.title: Which projector-coordinate constraint could exclude four bases?
targets.question: After checking the vector-coordinate obstruction, can a faithful projector formulation impose a dimension-six constraint stronger than m <= d+1?
targets.gap: The existing elementary projector bound permits four, five, six and seven bases at d=6. No stronger exclusion is supplied by that bound.
targets.next_step: Track polynomial degree before and after P=vv*. First reproduce the stated separation, then test exact certificates for a genuinely stronger constraint.
targets.success: A scope-correct formalization of the reported obstruction or a new certificate for the four-basis feasible set. Failure of one encoding is not nonexistence.

updates.title: Degree-Four Vector-Coordinate SoS Cannot Detect the MUB Upper Bound
updates.locator: Sections 8 to 10; consequences for Randomstrasse101 Open Problem 23
updates.note: The preprint reports a degree-four obstruction for the two specified vector-coordinate encodings. Centered projectors recover m <= d+1, which still allows four bases in dimension six. Neither result decides the fourth-basis question; no independent proof replay is claimed.

families.title: Do negative base-phi prefixes obey the trident classification?
families.question: Is each admissible negative-prefix occurrence sequence one Lucas-parameterized V_F, V_G or V_H component, or an allowed union of three components?
families.foothold: Exact golden return itineraries, gap spectra and Beatty displacement identities provide candidate tools.
families.gap: Negative-position base-phi digits need a value-preserving conversion, followed by an identification with the specific subshifts in the paper.
families.next_step: Port the two-sided expansion and the three sequence families with explicit union and multiplicity conventions.
families.success: The classification for every admissible prefix, or an exact necessary-invariant violation excluding all permitted parameterizations.

targets.title: A bounded-state negative-prefix transducer
targets.question: For each fixed prefix length m, can a finite-state transducer read canonical Zeckendorf input and output the first m negative-position base-phi digits?
targets.gap: Contractive intuition is insufficient: carry residues and a uniform reachable-state bound for fixed m need proof.
targets.next_step: Compute exact Z[phi] residue traces, propose a state invariant, and prove transition closure and output correctness.
targets.success: A finite machine with a proof for every canonical input at fixed m. Finite samples alone establish neither the state bound nor correctness.

targets.title: From negative cylinders to exact return itineraries
targets.question: Can each negative-prefix cylinder be identified with the paper's F, G or H itinerary, or its allowed three-component interleaving?
targets.gap: Existing golden-word return theorems apply only after the cylinder/subshift identification is established.
targets.next_step: Start with one admissible single-component prefix; derive its gap word and Lucas parameters by exact desubstitution.
targets.success: A quantified cylinder-to-itinerary equality and Lucas-parameter recursion. Record any violated gap or return-word invariant.

targets.title: Use the proved Kimberling criterion as a conversion check
targets.question: Can the exponent-doubling criterion in Shallit and Vukusic Theorem 5 be transported faithfully to the repository's exact two-sided phi representation?
targets.gap: The criterion is reported proved externally. Its formalization needs the same canonical digit and symmetry conventions and does not settle the trident conjecture.
targets.next_step: Port the symmetry and integer-value predicates, replay the exact algebraic criterion, and use it as a regression case for two-sided digit conversion.
targets.success: A faithful theorem-level bridge to a known result, with no claim of a new conjecture resolution.

updates.title: New properties of the φ-representation of integers
updates.note: The paper reports a proof of the exponent-doubling criterion for symmetric phi-representations. It supplies a conversion test case, not a proof of the general negative-prefix trident classification. The arXiv revision is March 2026, not its HTML generation date.

families.title: Does the Ordered Zeckendorf Long Game Strategy maximize length?
families.question: Among legal terminal runs starting from n copies of F_1, does the specified Long Game Strategy attain maximum length?
families.foothold: Value-preserving rewrites and canonical normal forms supply the forgetful arithmetic structure.
families.gap: Ordered states, the exact game orientation, path length and the meaning of arbitrary switch order require separate treatment.
families.next_step: Define the five ordered moves and resolve whether all switch tie choices are intended to be equally optimal.
families.success: A longest-path proof for the precise strategy semantics, or two exact legal runs witnessing a failure.

targets.title: Does switch-order freedom preserve LGS length?
targets.question: Do all allowed switch tie choices lead to the same LGS terminal length from the specified initial states?
targets.gap: The universal LGS statement depends on this interpretation; normal-form uniqueness does not imply equal run lengths.
targets.next_step: Enumerate exact ordered states and all switch tie choices for bounded n; retain differing lengths and full move traces.
targets.success: A switch-order independence proof, or an exact counterexample requiring a deterministic or existential reformulation.

targets.title: Height-preserving local exchanges for LGS
targets.question: Can each LGS priority choice be shown to attain an argmax successor of the longest-remaining-path Bellman recursion?
targets.gap: The game DAG needs its own termination proof. Local exchange lemmas may fail even when global optimality survives.
targets.next_step: Test swap-first, leftmost-one merge and rightmost-split exchanges against exact state heights; save both suffix witnesses at the first failure.
targets.success: Proved height dominance for every reachable strategy state, followed by well-founded induction. A failed exchange refutes that route only.

families.title: Do random Zeckendorf game lengths have a Gaussian limit?
families.question: Under a precisely specified random game measure, does the centered, variance-normalized length converge to a Gaussian?
families.foothold: Finite weighted probability, event counts and moments support exact bounded game calculations.
families.gap: Uniform terminal-path sampling and locally uniform move sampling give different measures. A limit theorem needs dependence control and nondegenerate variance.
families.next_step: Define both path measures exactly; prioritize the dossier's locally uniform mixing question with explicit quantifiers.
families.success: A limit theorem with its hypotheses discharged. Histograms and finite moment agreement remain empirical evidence.

targets.title: Two exact game-length generating functions
targets.question: Can exact finite recursions distinguish uniform terminal-path sampling from locally uniform successor sampling on the game DAG?
targets.gap: Move multiplicities and suffix-path counts affect transition weights. Treating the measures as interchangeable changes the target.
targets.next_step: Compute both rational generating functions independently on small value-preserving state DAGs, with the terminal state contributing 1.
targets.success: Proved recursions, normalization and moment identities for both measures, including an explicit comparison example.

targets.title: A uniform regenerative-barrier estimate
targets.question: Can a canonical digit barrier bound the dependence of separated split indicators uniformly over initial input size?
targets.gap: Finite carry locality need not survive conditioning on entire random histories. The relevant mixing-CLT summability and variance hypotheses must be checked explicitly.
targets.next_step: Search exact history pairs that share a proposed barrier, then measure and bound influence-crossing events under the chosen measure.
targets.success: An explicit uniform mixing estimate strong enough for the selected CLT, or a minimal history pair invalidating the proposed barrier.

families.title: Can a prime have equal Fibonacci periods modulo p and p²?
families.question: Does a prime p exist with pi(p) = pi(p²), where pi is the Pisano period? The infinitely-many assertion is a separate stronger question.
families.foothold: Golden-unit powers, Fibonacci coordinates, apparition ranks and split/inert arithmetic connect the mod-p side.
families.gap: The exceptional lift from p to p² is missing. A finite search with no examples does not refute existence.
families.next_step: Identify recurrence period, matrix order and golden-unit order before studying the first lift defect.
families.success: A verified prime witness or a universal nonexistence proof. Keep local bridge theorems separate from the global existence question.

targets.title: Pisano period as matrix and golden-unit order
targets.question: For m >= 2, can the pair-recurrence period be proved equal to the multiplicative order of A = [[0,1],[1,1]] over Z/mZ and of its golden-unit representation?
targets.gap: Matrix order concerns the whole matrix, so equality with the orbit period needs proof; invertibility and indexing must be explicit.
targets.next_step: Prove the Fibonacci formula for A^n and compare the return condition (F_n,F_(n+1)) = (0,1) modulo m.
targets.success: A reusable equivalence for all m >= 2, with small-modulus conventions stated and checked.

targets.title: The first-lift defect criterion modulo p²
targets.question: With r = pi(p) and A^r = I + pB modulo p², is pi(p²) equal to r exactly when B vanishes modulo p, and otherwise equal to pr?
targets.gap: The argument requires the reduction-order relation and a justified calculation of the order of I+pB, including small primes.
targets.next_step: Define B as a residue class, prove the kernel-order dichotomy, and cross-check recurrence and matrix computations independently.
targets.success: A proved local lift dichotomy with every prime case covered. This does not settle whether a vanishing defect ever occurs.

families.title: How large is maximum order complexity along polynomial inputs?
families.question: For the parity of the Zeckendorf digit sum along n², can maximum order complexity of the first N terms be bounded above by C N^(1/4) for all sufficiently large N?
families.foothold: Canonical digit normalization and factor tools support exact repeated-block analysis.
families.gap: Factor complexity is a different invariant. The upper bound needs a uniform successor-determinism or carry-state argument.
families.next_step: Implement the exact finite repeated-block criterion before attempting an effective carry-window bound.
families.success: A quantified upper bound with constants and threshold, or a counterexample to a stated effective bound. Finite scaling plots do not settle the exponent.

targets.title: An exact successor-collision certificate
targets.question: Can finite maximum order complexity be certified by equal-length block collisions and their following bits, including degenerate constant-prefix cases?
targets.gap: Off-by-one conventions and special zero-memory cases must match the source definition.
targets.next_step: Cross-check a naive implementation against a suffix-based method; emit equal blocks with unequal successors for every claimed lower bound.
targets.success: A proved finite criterion and replayable witnesses, independent of any conjectured asymptotic exponent.

targets.title: Can bounded carry state force the next parity bit?
targets.question: For square inputs, can a history of length O(N^(1/4)) determine enough boundary carry information to determine the next Zeckendorf digit-sum parity?
targets.gap: Unbounded carry propagation and noninjective history-to-state maps are possible obstructions.
targets.next_step: Track exact normalization of 2nh+h² at Fibonacci/Lucas scales, then search for equal observed histories with conflicting next bits.
targets.success: An explicit uniform boundary-state theorem implying the upper bound, or exact witness pairs falsifying the proposed window.

families.title: Do genuine lowest Weil modes converge to Xi?
families.question: Do suitably normalized Fourier transforms of genuine lowest Weil modes converge locally uniformly to the Riemann Xi function as the physical support grows?
families.foothold: FixedScaleWeilQuadraticForm exposes the actual finite prime-power and Archimedean multiplier. Its zero-sum formula has explicit convergence and ZeroData premises; it supplies no ground-mode limit.
families.gap: An explicit prolate model and a finite-window certificate leave actual-mode identification, full-space coercivity and a growing-window comparison to establish.
families.next_step: Reuse the existing Weil research lanes. Match operator domains, physical window, normalization and Fourier convention before comparing any two certificates.
families.success: A quantitative estimate for the same genuine family tending to zero on every compact set, combined with the correctly normalized model limit. A fixed-window residual is one input.

targets.title: Compare one genuine mode and its actual candidate
targets.question: Can a full-space residual and complement-coercivity certificate bound the Fourier error for the same physical Weil operator and prolate trial?
targets.gap: A retained matrix residual leaves an exterior term. Domain error and candidate normalization must be paid separately.
targets.next_step: Check the existing numerical and proof-script outputs before creating another certificate; assemble prime, pole, Gamma and tail terms with one set of parameters.
targets.success: An independently replayable fixed-window bound with every premise identified. It should not be relabelled as a uniform all-window theorem.

targets.title: A physical-window rate for the true mode error
targets.question: Can arithmetic cancellation and complement coercivity control the actual-mode Fourier error along an unbounded sequence of support windows?
targets.gap: Increasing numerical precision or an exterior cutoff does not reduce the physical error by itself; gaps may deteriorate with the window.
targets.next_step: Separate the physical window, finite matrix dimension and numerical tail cutoff. Seek bounds uniform over each target compact set with an explicit vanishing budget.
targets.success: A rate for the genuine family with all growth terms retained, or an obstruction to the particular proposed estimate.

source.title: Zeta Spectral Triples
source.locator: Sections 7 and 8; the explicit-model limit and the actual lowest-mode approximation
source.note: This is a 2025 source rechecked alongside the June 2026 Suzuki paper. The explicit model limit and convergence of genuine lowest modes are separate. Finite spectral agreement is not an all-scale proof.

updates.title: Weil's quadratic form via the screw function
updates.locator: Corollary 1.6, equation (1.12); discussion following it; Section 7
updates.note: The limit is conjectural; Corollary 1.6 proves an implication from it. Section 7 assumes RH for its heuristic. That assumption cannot be imported into an unconditional proof of the limit.

families.title: Does Suzuki's boundary characteristic satisfy the zeta limit?
families.question: Can theta(a) and a nonvanishing normalization make W(a,theta;z) approach z² xi(1/2-iz)/xi'(1/2-iz) in the sense intended by equation (1.12)?
families.foothold: FiniteResolventClarkIdentity transports an explicitly supplied paired atomic spectrum. The fixed-scale Weil multiplier is another input. Neither identifies the actual boundary characteristic or its limiting measure.
families.gap: The spectral shift lambda < lambda_a, the physical characteristic function and the treatment of poles in compact-uniform convergence need explicit control.
families.next_step: First resolve the analytic meaning of the meromorphic quotient and normalization. Then identify the paper's W with a repository operator construction without supplying zeta zeros as spectral input.
families.success: A precise faithful limit statement and proof without RH premises. The conditional implication in Corollary 1.6 is already a source result.

targets.title: Identify the actual finite-window characteristic
targets.question: Can the paper's deficiency-space boundary characteristic be identified with a resolvent or Fredholm construction using the genuine screw kernel?
targets.gap: A finite atomic measure chosen to look like a Clark measure does not establish this identification.
targets.next_step: Fix the domain, boundary convention and inner product; derive the relevant boundary function and measure rather than assume their desired expansion.
targets.success: An operator-to-characteristic identity on a specified analytic domain with normalization constants retained.

targets.title: Control the spectral shift without assuming RH
targets.question: Can the shift needed to define the window Hilbert spaces be controlled as a grows, without assuming positivity of every Weil window?
targets.gap: The source's global Hilbert-space heuristic assumes RH. Finiteness of prime terms at each fixed a gives no uniform estimate.
targets.next_step: Use explicit lower bounds and compare shifted constructions on common test-function cores; track any effect on characteristic zeros and normalization.
targets.success: A shift-control lemma with unconditional hypotheses useful for the proposed limit, or a precise failure of a proposed normalization.

source.title: Weil's quadratic form via the screw function
source.locator: Corollary 1.6, equation (1.12); discussion following it; Section 7
source.note: The limit is conjectural; Corollary 1.6 proves an implication from it. Section 7 assumes RH for its heuristic. That assumption cannot be imported into an unconditional proof of the limit.

families.title: Is real phase retrieval exponentially ill-conditioned at 2M-1 measurements?
families.question: For every full-spark real (2M-1)-by-M matrix, M>1, do universal C>0 and beta in (0,1) bound omega(A) by C times the maximum row norm times beta^M?
families.foothold: IsNormalizedRankOneProjection and trace-overlap geometry supply a quadratic-readout vocabulary. A full-spark rectangular frame, its singular values and the modulus measurement map still need an explicit bridge.
families.gap: The Gaussian asymptotic reported in July is a random-matrix result. The target quantifies over every admissible deterministic matrix.
families.next_step: Reduce the full-spark omega definition to minimum singular value over square row submatrices, retaining row scaling, then test candidate deterministic inequalities.
families.success: A universal normalized bound for all dimensions and frames, or a family refuting all proposed universal constants. A finite numerical example cannot decide the asymptotic claim.

targets.title: An exact square-submatrix formulation of omega
targets.question: Under full spark at N=2M-1, is omega(A) exactly the minimum of sigma_min(A_T) over M-row sets T?
targets.gap: The source definition also allows larger row sets; its equivalence needs a rank and Loewner-order argument.
targets.next_step: Formalize rectangular row restriction and the variational least singular value. Preserve M>1 and the source's complement-rank convention.
targets.success: A reusable equivalence with a row-rescaling test and exact small cases. This is a formalization bridge, not a new resolution.

targets.title: A deterministic obstruction stronger than a Gaussian example
targets.question: Can row-subset geometry force an exponentially small least singular value uniformly over every normalized full-spark frame?
targets.gap: Average-case small-ball estimates and the existence of a badly conditioned example do not imply a worst-case upper bound.
targets.next_step: Compare extremal deterministic families using certified spectral intervals; seek a packing, determinant or partition argument with dimension-independent constants.
targets.success: A uniform inequality or a counterfamily for a stated effective bound, with numerical probes kept separate from the universal claim.

source.title: Randomstrasse101: Open Problems of 2025
source.note: Conjecture 20 is the universal full-spark statement. The lower-case n in the displayed complement-rank formula is read as the column dimension M; the normalized domain is stated explicitly here.

updates.title: Extreme least singular values of Gaussian row submatrices and a phase retrieval stability problem
updates.locator: Abstract and main Gaussian row-submatrix theorem; N=2m-1 specialization
updates.note: The source reports omega(A_m)=4^(-m+o_P(m)) for real Gaussian matrices. This addresses the Gaussian question in Open Problem 21, not the universal deterministic Conjecture 20. Its proof has not been independently replayed here.

families.title: Does injectivity at 4M-5 complex measurements become rare?
families.question: For M>=2 and a Haar-random M-plane in C^(4M-5), let p_M be the probability that x modulo global phase maps injectively to |Ax|². Is p_M<1 for each M, and does p_M tend to zero?
families.foothold: The repository's rank-one projection predicates and trace geometry are a foothold for lifting intensity measurements to Hermitian matrices. They do not provide the random-frame probability theorem.
families.gap: Generic injectivity, existence of one exceptional injective frame, and injectivity probability are distinct. The old universal 4M-4 necessity statement is already false.
families.next_step: Encode the measurement kernel on actual differences xx* - yy*. Define the Grassmannian measure and bad event before relying on dimension counts.
families.success: A nonzero bad-event probability for each M and a separate asymptotic bound proving the limit. An isolated example does not establish a probability.

targets.title: A faithful Hermitian lift of equal-intensity pairs
targets.question: Is equal intensity equivalent to the linear measurement map annihilating xx* - yy*, with zero difference exactly global-phase equivalence?
targets.gap: Unnormalized signals and the zero vector need explicit treatment. Arbitrary rank-two matrices are not automatically differences with the required inertia.
targets.next_step: Prove the trace identity and represent the difference cone exactly; relate normalized nonzero signals to the rank-one projector predicate.
targets.success: A bidirectional statement preserving all signals, not just unit-norm or generic vectors.

targets.title: From an algebraic witness to positive probability
targets.question: Can a noninjective-frame witness be extended to a positive-measure set at the critical measurement count?
targets.gap: A single real-algebraic solution may lie in a measure-zero stratum. Dimension counting alone does not settle transversality or probability.
targets.next_step: Analyze the rank-two difference incidence set on a concrete Grassmannian chart and verify a local persistence or measure argument.
targets.success: A proved positive-measure bad set for a stated dimension or a uniform probabilistic estimate; retain the distinction between the two conjecture clauses.

source.title: Randomstrasse101: Open Problems of 2025
source.note: The statement is recorded in the checked survey. The 11-measurement example in C^4 refutes the older necessity claim, not these two probability clauses. This entry does not assert exhaustive absence of later work.

families.title: Do SIC-POVMs exist in every positive dimension?
families.question: Does every positive dimension d admit d² unit vectors forming an equiangular tight frame, equivalently a SIC-POVM?
families.foothold: WeylDisplacementTrace supplies displacement trace orthogonality; the rank-one projector predicate supplies individual projectors. A displacement basis alone does not construct a SIC fiducial.
families.gap: For d>1 the target requires squared overlaps 1/(d+1) and sum of rank-one projectors dI. This is distinct from the MUB version of Zauner's conjecture.
families.next_step: Connect the existing displacement operators to a precisely normalized fiducial system, keeping every extra symmetry and number-theoretic premise explicit.
families.success: An unconditional construction in every dimension. Exact isolated dimensions or a construction under Stark-type assumptions retain their narrower scope.

targets.title: From a verified fiducial to a SIC orbit
targets.question: Can exact displacement-overlap equations for a unit fiducial imply the d²-vector equiangular tight-frame and POVM identities?
targets.gap: Trace orthogonality is available but the orbit normalization, distinctness and identity resolution must be derived.
targets.next_step: Use the existing displacement composition and trace owners; derive twirling and the orbit Gram entries rather than introducing another Weyl convention.
targets.success: A conditional fiducial-to-SIC theorem with d and phase conventions explicit, plus exact low-dimensional checks.

targets.title: An exact certificate behind a numerical SIC candidate
targets.question: Can a proposed algebraic fiducial be certified against all required overlap and normalization equations?
targets.gap: A small floating residual does not establish equality or existence. An imposed order-three symmetry narrows the search class.
targets.next_step: Use explicit number-field embeddings and exact polynomial reductions; list which equations and embedding choices are certified.
targets.success: A verified instance with its dimension and assumptions, never presented as the universal existence theorem.

source.title: Randomstrasse101: Open Problems of 2025
source.note: The survey records the SIC existence conjecture and conditional number-theoretic progress. Neither those assumptions nor the MUB conjecture are identified with an unconditional all-dimension SIC proof.

families.title: Does the expected Lovasz number of random circulants approach sqrt(n)?
families.question: For dense undirected random circulant graphs with independent Bernoulli(1/2) choices of nonzero step pairs {k,-k}, is E theta(G)=(1+o(1)) sqrt(n)?
families.foothold: FinitePoisson supplies standard characters and the character-group equivalence on ZMod n. This is the correct finite Fourier group for circulant symmetrization.
families.gap: The finite Fourier reduction does not remove the remaining probabilistic loss. A theta SDP, normalization bridge and random-graph model must be connected explicitly.
families.next_step: Derive the cyclic averaging and Fourier-diagonal reduction with the repository character convention; then attach sound primal and dual bounds.
families.success: A proof of the expected leading constant, or a rigorous conflicting asymptotic. Numerical optimization on finitely many graph sizes is exploratory.

targets.title: A normalization-safe circulant theta reduction
targets.question: Can cyclic averaging identify the theta SDP with a finite Fourier positivity problem without changing its optimum?
targets.gap: The SDP uses trace one while a scaled first-row LP can use x_0=1. Confusing these conventions changes the objective by n.
targets.next_step: Prove averaging preserves PSD, edge constraints and objective, then derive eigenvalues using the existing ZMod characters, with sign and scale recorded.
targets.success: A bidirectional feasible-point translation and equality of objectives under the chosen normalization.

targets.title: Certified bounds for a concrete circulant graph
targets.question: Can explicit primal and dual witnesses give rigorous theta bounds for a supplied circulant graph?
targets.gap: Solver tolerance and approximate Fourier eigenvalues can falsely certify feasibility. Real algebraic or interval enclosures need a soundness theorem.
targets.next_step: Construct exact small-graph witnesses and certified residual margins; test graph-complement and scaling conventions independently.
targets.success: Replayable upper and lower bounds with all rounding budgets. These are finite footholds for the expectation conjecture.
